title: Observability weekly - 2026-06-22
content:
Week of 2026-06-22 — Observability team weekly notes

Summary:
- Primary focus this week: finalizing cost-telemetry ingestion path, rolling out the new tracing sampling rules, and stabilizing the new model-serving dashboards ahead of Dedicated launch next month.
- No high-severity incidents; one ongoing regression in the KV cache exporter that is causing noise in cost attribution (see action items).

Highlights / Progress:
1) Tracing
- Deployed new adaptive sampling changes to Jaeger/OTEL collector in prod (canary on 3 nodes): sampling now uses a combination of service-level QPS and error rates to increase retention for errors and important request paths (OBS-412).
- Early effects: error trace retention up ~45% for low-volume services (good), overall trace volume down ~18% which reduces storage and query costs.
- Follow-up: implement a lightweight trace header passthrough so downstream services can opt-in to full sampling for debugging sessions. Miguel to prototype by 2026-07-01.

2) Dashboards
- New per-model-serving dashboard (model-serving-overview) created in Grafana: p95/p99 response time, tokens/sec, active streams, and per-route cost estimate panel. KPIs validated against tracing metrics.
- Added an Alerts section: two new alerts pushed for p99 > 800ms sustained 5m and model-serving-error-rate > 1% sustained 3m. Alerts have temp 30-min notification windows to cut down on flapping during autoscale.
- Polishing: panel description fields and runbook links are still WIP. Lena to finish documentation + runbooks by 2026-06-29.

3) Cost telemetry
- Ingestion pipeline: landed schema v2 for cost attribution which attaches token counts and approximate GPU-seconds to spans. Initial upstream PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/98.
- Current problem: the KV cache exporter sometimes double-counts when cache hits are recorded by both runtime and proxy -> affects per-route cost estimates (~5–8% inflation on some routes). Rajesh is debugging; temporary fix deployed that dedups by span attribute. Expect final fix by 2026-06-25.
- Unit economics dashboard: first draft shows cost-per-1M-tokens by model family. Early numbers: small models ~ $2.3 / 1M tokens, large models (from on-prem pools) ~ $19 / 1M tokens (include GPU amortization assumptions). This will be refined as Dedicated bills come in.

Standup highlights (this week's notable items):
- Aisha: coordinated canary of adaptive sampling, helped triage collector CPU spikes on canary nodes (root cause: sidecar config mismatches).
- Miguel: started prototype for trace header passthrough; collected test vectors from solutions-eng.
- Lena: onboarded dashboard feedback from SRE and Solutions Eng; iterated on panel layouts.
- Rajesh: investigating KV exporter double-counting; added dedupe filter to temporary pipeline.
- Claire: updated alerting playbook and created escalation doc for cost regression alerts.

Incidents / Postmortems
- No Sev1/2 incidents this week. Noted increased alert noise from low-volume model endpoints after sampling change; adjusted alert thresholds and added a short suppression window while we monitor.

Decisions made
- Keep adaptive sampling in prod canary for 2 weeks before full rollout (agreed after sync 2026-06-22).
- Temporarily route cost telemetry ingestion through a dedupe layer rather than reverting schema v2. This minimizes data loss and gives us time to fix exporter logic.

Action items (owner — due):
- Rajesh Kumar — finalize exporter dedupe fix and add unit tests (due 2026-06-25) [blocks accurate per-route cost].
- Lena Thompson — complete dashboard runbooks and link to alert pages (due 2026-06-29).
- Miguel Santos — prototype trace header passthrough and demo in Wednesday sync (due 2026-07-01).
- Aisha Patel — coordinate full rollout plan for adaptive sampling and schedule cross-team review with platform-engineering (due 2026-07-02).
- Claire Huang — add cost regression alert to oncall rotation and create incident playbook snippet for cost surprises (due 2026-06-26).

Blockers / Risks
- KV cache double-counting risk inflates per-route cost; could mislead sales/finance if presented prematurely. Mitigation: add clear footnote to unit-econ dashboard and hold formal reporting until confirm fix.
- Dashboard query performance: one heavy query for per-route token breakdown is causing slow dashboard loads during peak. Solution path: pre-aggregate hourly rollups and move heavy joins to the OLAP cube (OBS-421).

Meetings / Syncs
- Weekly observability sync — Tue 2026-06-23 10:30am PT (attendees: all collaborators). Agenda: adaptive sampling canary review, dashboard signoff, cost telemetry rollout timeline.
- Cross-team review with platform-eng scheduled 2026-07-02 to discuss rollout SLAs for Dedicated.

Notes / Miscellany
- Linked PRs and docs: OBS-412 (adaptive sampling), OBS-421 (cost-rollup), telemetry PR #98.
- Suggested TODO: engage finance to validate cost-per-1M-tokens assumptions before sending to sales (Aisha to own outreach).

Next week preview (2026-06-29):
- Finish exporter fix and validate corrected cost numbers; update unit-econ dashboard.
- Complete dashboard runbooks and open training slot for Solutions Eng.
- Decide on full or staged rollout of adaptive sampling based on canary metrics (target decision 2026-07-02).


Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (as of 2026-06-22):
- Total traces/day (sampled): 24.6M (down 18% vs last week)
- Error-trace retention: +45% for low-volume services after adaptive sampling
- Per-route cost estimate variance (pre-fix): up to +8% on affected routes
- Dashboard load p95: 1.4s (investigating heavy query)

If anything here looks wrong or you want a deeper breakdown (eg. raw query examples, collector configs), ping on #eng-observability or add to linked artifacts.
